title: Subbing for Johnny Hodges one night with Duke Ellington
summary: Thomas played the parts for Hodges at a Fifth Avenue club beside Harry Carney, and Hinton recalls his own night with Duke.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So what did you say? Whose band is this?
What happened before ...(?)...? Johnny was sick or something?
Yeah, they called me to play in his place.

Yeah. I didn't have to play any of the solos. I just had to play the part. I always appreciated Johnny. He just showed me where to play and where to lay out? See, the guys knew where all those solos came, so somebody else would take the solos. But it a great experience. I got through it all right.
We was playing that club on Fifth Avenue.
They had a Jazz club there for a little while on Fifth Avenue, and Duke Ellington played in it. It was somewhere between the Forties and Fifties. It was a club downstairs.
No. That place didn't last long. They just had Duke there...
On Fifth Avenue or Sixth Avenue? Or Seventh Avenue...
No, it was on Fifth Avenue. I remember that clearly. It didn't last long. It was a club that somebody had gotten (?), and Duke would draw anywhere...
So you say you were sitting next to Harry Carney?
Well, what happened? You didn't play a solo; you just had to play the parts.
Yeah, I had to play the parts.
Harry was very kind to you, huh?

Mmm-hmm. Because somebody else would... They knew where the solos would come in, and somebody else would take Johnny's solo. And Duke almost went crazy, man, when he left the band; and he kept on until he got them back. Because I know, we used to book Johnny Hodges when he had small bands. And he finally got Ben Webster back, too.

Well, his band was great because he had great musicians. He had so many stars. People like Bubber Miley and Tricky Sam...
So that was the one night that you played in the band, huh?
I played one night in that band, too, only one night, at the Rainbow Grill. Joe Benjamin had been sick, and I worked one night with ...(? )... It was one of the greatest experiences of my life.
